messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: seed in RStan (vs Stan)
parts:
There are some difference between RStan and Stan in terms of how the seed is used. In RStan, I think taking a look at sampler_command in
https://code.google.com/p/stan/source/browse/rstan/rstan/inst/include/rstan/stan_fit.hpp
will help you.  I can remember there are at least tow differences:
1. initial values, in RStan, it is initialized once 
2. reset seed before sampling. (Line 475) 

So I think if you reset the seed in Stan before sampling, you might be able to get the same behavior. 

--
Jiqiang

I didn't realize that the code was copied over. Bob added a few lines
of code that may solve a lot of those problems. I don't think we
realized that the change needed to be made in two places. See lines
346 to 369 in src/stan/gm/command.hpp.

Those lines should be included in stan_fit.hpp after 454.

If this code is being shared, I think we should pull out the common
code and maintain it in one place.



Daniel

parts:
If you have a rstan rolled from master, you can do this in R

library(rstan)
example(stan_demo)
library(parallel)
models <- mclapply(1:83, mc.cores = 8, FUN = function(m) mean(unlist(get_logposterior(stan_demo(m, chains = 1, refresh = -1, seed = 12345), inc_warmup = TRUE)))) # better to use clang++ here
names(models) <- model_names
which(sapply(models, FUN = function(m) !is.na(m) && is.infinite(m)))
oxford  salm2   salm 
    32     36     37 


So, those three are suspicious. The oxford model throws many

Warning (non-fatal rejection): Error in function stan::prob::binomial_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Probability parameter is -nan:0, but must be finite!

The salm and salm2 models throw many

Warning (non-fatal rejection): Error in function stan::prob::normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variable is nan:0, but must not be nan!

In contrast, command-line Stan does not show a problem (each was run with --seed=12345).

> @Daniel, it would be nice if we could execute make SEED=12345 test-models to
> use that SEED always, which would make it easier to do these comparisons
> with rstan

Sorry, that's pretty hard to do. The models aren't run from the
makefile. They are run from within google test using popen().

The good news: if you've already run test-models, you can just run the
model using the seed you want. The executables are all built and ready
to go.
